title: Gate B: a recorded turn replayed in ours, report in parity/gate-b/<trace>.json
gate: npm run gate:b (CI: gate.yml); 59/63 over 4 turns, all on oracle 0.79.3; a lower count fails
evidence: scripts/gate-b.mjs plays traces/2026-11-10-{say-hi,say-hi-2,storage} and 2026-11-09-long-answer through /gate-b/<trace> (server/replay.ts as Barkpark's runtime stream, the real hook and transcript); moments timed in-page. Proof it fails: the working line's exit delayed 100 -> 300 ms took it to 27/37 and --ci exited 1. Since 2026-11-09 each moment counts from the arrival that caused it (the stand-in's lateness under load is not the UI's): +200 ms in the UI before the own bubble fails it (624 ms), +300 ms on the stand-in's send answer does not (raw 727, counted 422). The replay also plays the fleet stream's state flips at the oracle rail's times (on 0.79.3, which shows no Working on the open bot, at the working line's); the transcript's time row is not read as the working line; a budget the oracle itself misses is not judged, and the report says so. Since 2026-11-10 a trace is not judged once its recipe is re-recorded on a newer oracle version (scripts/lib/turn-traces.mjs; every turn trace names oracle_version, record.mjs writes it): the three 0.79.2 traces of 2026-11-08 are printed as superseded, their rail:working misses gone with them; npm run check refuses a record left for one. The page's window has focus as the oracle's had (CDP focus emulation), and the tile's Unread dot is a moment (rail:unread; say-hi 6521 vs 6524 ms, storage 4228 vs 4231 ms). Proof it fails: focus flipped took it to 51/63 (the dot missing on 2 turns, an extra dot on the other 2). The 4 misses left are label:status, one per turn.
